Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our vendor approval process, our InfoSec team has a couple of focused asks on the CAIQ items you submitted earlier. We need a concise mapping to evidence for two areas that are blocking our security review:

- Data residency / customer-controlled data location (CAIQ C-07, C-08 related controls)
- Network segmentation & tenant isolation (CAIQ N-10 / logical separation controls)

Can you provide: (1) the specific control IDs from your CAIQ mapping that cover these topics, (2) the exact evidence file names we should review, and (3) a short description of how Redwood enforces the controls (1–3 bullets each).

If possible, can you share the artifacts by EOD Friday 24-Apr? We can route them to our GRC review and finish procurement.

Appreciate it — Jordan

Subject: Re: Initial CAIQ ask — data residency & segmentation evidence

Jordan —

Attaching the short narrative for the Data Residency controls. Highlighted points:

• CAIQ controls mapped: C-07 (Data Location), C-08 (Data Lifecycle & Transfers).
• Evidence files: evidence-pack-2026-04.zip -> "residency/region-pin-policy.pdf", "residency/kms-scope.txt".
• How we enforce:
  - Customer may pin workloads to a specific region via the Console or API; we persist pin in the deployment manifest and enforce placement at the orchestration layer.
  - KMS keys are customer-scoped when requested; we support both Redwood-managed and customer-managed keys (BYOK) with KMS policies limiting decrypt to region-bound instances.
  - Backups and snapshot retention are stored in region-specific object storage buckets; replication across regions only occurs if explicitly enabled in the tenant config.

Let me know if you want redlines or a formal attestation document; we can provide a signed statement for procurement.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett

Jordan / team —

Pushed the network artifacts into the evidence zip and included a short summary below:

• CAIQ controls mapped: N-10 (Network Isolation), N-11 (Firewalling & Perimeter Controls).
• Evidence files: redwood_network_diagram.pdf, evidence-pack-2026-04.zip -> "network/tenant-isolation.md", "network/nsq-firewall-rules.txt".
• Implementation highlights:
  - Logical tenant separation: multi-tenant runtime enforces per-tenant namespaces plus strict RBAC at control-plane APIs; network-level policies deny cross-tenant overlay routing by default.
  - VPC isolation for dedicated/private deployments: customers get dedicated VPCs and optional physical segregation on Dedicated clusters.
  - East-west segmentation: microservice mesh enforces mTLS and layer-7 policies; we use service Identity tokens to avoid relying solely on IP ranges.

If CapitolHealth wants a deeper walkthrough of the firewall rule extracts, Marissa can book time with your infra team and share a sanitized sample config.

— Rishi
